# RETRO: PR #12254 (team 2)

## What worked
- Tracing where the menu action's process actually lives exposed that the PR's causal explanation does not match the source; a neutral follow-up to Sol independently confirmed it.
- Source-only review of systemd/uwsm resolved the scheduling questions without touching the live session.

## Process deviations
- Coordinator: `pi_job.py wait` output includes `latest_text`, which showed Sol's one-line closing summary before the Opus final existed. Incidental headline read; not disclosed to Opus. Improvement: have `pi_job.py wait/status` omit `latest_text` (or add a `--lifecycle-only` flag) so pre-final monitoring stays lifecycle-only.
- Opus: pre-execution inventory assumed `omarchy-osd` was absent from the sandbox PATH; the host `/usr/bin/omarchy-osd` ran inside the sandbox during the plain test run. No effect (cleared env, read-only root, no bus sockets); run 2 confirmed byte-identical to head copies. Improvement carried into brief template: gate a PATH probe before any test child and stub every unmocked command.
- Opus filtered blank lines in two systemd source reads to fit the output bound (no content dropped, no width projection).

## Carry forward
- Briefs for session/power actions should explicitly name nested sessions sharing the host user manager as unsafe (uwsm stop uses the user session bus).
- Tool note: `pi_job.py verify` works well; Sol finished in 7 min, follow-up in 5 min.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The change is correct and brings logout in line with reboot and shutdown. `uwsm stop` now runs as its own transient unit in the systemd user manager, outside the caller's process tree. If scheduling fails, the script exits before the OSD and before any window is closed. One point remains open: the source does not show that this resolves the menu logout failure in #12233.

| | Reboot / shutdown | Logout (base) | Logout (this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scheduling | `systemd-run --user --collect --quiet --on-active=2s --timer-property=AccuracySec=100ms` | `nohup bash -c "sleep 2 && uwsm stop" &` | same `systemd-run` flags as reboot / shutdown |
| Where the delayed action runs | own user-manager unit | child of the calling process | own user-manager unit |
| Scheduling failure | exit before OSD and window closing | not detected; windows still closed | exit before OSD and window closing |

**Verified (repository test):** In an isolated sandbox, `test/shell.d/system-power-test.sh` passes on the PR head. It fails as expected against the base logout script and when `|| exit 1` is removed from the new logout script.

### "Fixes #12233" is not demonstrated for the menu path

The PR description attributes the failure to the invoking systemd scope being reaped when the script exits or the terminal closes. On the path reported in #12233 (menu > System > Logout), the source does not show any step that would kill the old delayed job:

```text
uwsm start ... hyprland.desktop
└─ wayland-wm@hyprland.desktop.service   (compositor unit)
   └─ Hyprland: hl.exec_cmd("omarchy-launch-shell")      fork + exec, no new unit
      └─ systemd-cat -- quickshell                         execs, no new unit
         └─ Util.execDetached -> bash -lc omarchy-system-logout
            └─ nohup bash -c "sleep 2 && uwsm stop" &    (base script)
               stays in the compositor unit's cgroup; no terminal scope involved
```

A systemd scope is not stopped when one of its processes exits. It stays alive while any process remains in it. Closing the other windows does not stop the compositor unit either. On this path the base job should therefore survive to run `uwsm stop`, so the actual cause of #12233 is still unknown. The new scheduling removes any dependence on the caller's lifetime and is sound hardening for other contexts, such as a terminal whose scope is stopped. It would not help if `uwsm stop` runs and then fails to stop the compositor.

**Impact:** Closing #12233 on the basis of this PR could leave the reported failure in place if its cause lies outside the caller-lifetime class.

**Suggested change:** Confirm with one real menu logout on a disposable machine or VM before treating #12233 as fixed. Alternatively, on an affected system with the old script, `journalctl -b -t uwsm` shows "Stopping compositor..." only if the delayed `uwsm stop` ran. With the new script, `journalctl --user -b -u 'run-*'` shows the scheduled unit's output. A nested compositor session that shares the user's systemd user manager is not a safe test bed: `uwsm stop` would stop the outer session's compositor. The second sentence of the new code comment ("nohup only survives SIGHUP; ...") describes removed code and could be dropped, which would also match the reboot and shutdown comments.

**Optional test improvement:** The test mocks only `systemd-run`, `omarchy-state`, `omarchy-hyprland-window-close-all` and `sleep`. `uwsm`, `systemctl` and `omarchy-osd` resolve to the real commands. In the sandbox, running this test against the base logout script reached a real `uwsm stop` through the background `nohup` job. On a live desktop, the same run (for example to confirm the test fails on the base, or during `git bisect`) would end the session, and any run on an Omarchy desktop shows real "Logging out", "Rebooting" and "Shutting down" OSD toasts. Adding logging stubs for `uwsm`, `systemctl` and `omarchy-osd` to `mock_bin` would make such cases fail safely. It would also let the expected logs assert that the OSD follows scheduling and is skipped on failure.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head `9c49736` against base `quattro` (`9c5482c`), including systemd `systemd-run`, timer, scope and service source (v258 and v261), uwsm v0.26.7 (the version in #12233), and the Hyprland and Quickshell spawn paths. The repository test ran in an isolated sandbox with no access to a user manager, session bus or desktop session. No real logout was performed, and the reporter's installed Hyprland, Quickshell and systemd builds and local session configuration were not examined.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
